steps.text: In a medium saucepan, combine water, bouillon, and spinach. Bring to a boil, and cook until spinach is tender.

Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Stir in flour, and cook for 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in milk. Season with minced onion, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened. Stir in spinach mixture.

raw_recipe.headline: Cream of Spinach Soup
raw_recipe.description: Sauteed chopped spinach is added to a roux-thickened mixture of milk and chicken bouillon for a fast and easy-to-prepare soup. This technique works well with a variety of vegetables.
raw_recipe.name: Cream of Spinach Soup

recipeInstructions.text: In a medium saucepan, combine water, bouillon, and spinach. Bring to a boil, and cook until spinach is tender.

Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Stir in flour, and cook for 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in milk. Season with minced onion, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened. Stir in spinach mixture.

review.reviewBody:
I have made this recipe twice, and I love it. There are several things I did the second time around that made it better (all gathered from other reviewers)

1. I used about 1 lb of fresh spinach and blended the spinach mixture.
2. Used 2 cups milk & 1 cup heavy cream
3. Used fresh onion and garlic
4. Added a dash of Celery Salt, Cayanne Pepper, nutmeg, and thyme
5. Mixed in about 1/4 cup Parmasean Cheese.

Most of these ideas came from other reviews. Combining them all together makes a really good soup (and not bland at all).

This is a delicious soup! My family loves lots of flavor, so I used 4 bouillon cubes vs. 3, used a heaping tablespoon of the dried minced onion, and included a light shake of garlic powder as well. This was the second or third time I've made this and was unable to find the frozen chopped spinach. As a substitute, I used 16 oz. of fresh spinach with the stems pinched off, cooked with the recipe-specified amount of water and bouillon (cooked, covered, on High for 3 minutes); and used added to soup as recipe specified. Fabulous!

This was a great recipe. I made this with fresh onion and garlic sautéed in butter. Added the flour and then the bouillon and water. I used 2-12 ounce bags frozen cauliflower and used two cups of cream and two cups of milk. I also added a pinch of celery salt, cayenne pepper, thyme, nutmeg. I used half a cup of shaker parm too. At the end I used an immersion blender and it came out super creamy! Although it was tweaked a lot it was still super easy and delicious.

I loved this soup and I know my daughter will love it when she tries it too! I did follow what other reviewers did except I did use over a pound of fresh spinach and whatever I had left of celery in 2 cups of water. I would use 3 chic bouillon next time but add no salt or 2 chic bouillon cubes and little salt. The salts from the celery was enough so if yiu decide tonuse celery I would suggest to not use any salt. I made the rue as other reviewers suggested, with milk and heavy cream I used 2.5 cups 1% milk and half cup heavy cream. I sautéed onions and garlic in the butter then a stirred in flour and adding 1 cup at a time of the milk as I consistently whisked. I added sslt, pepper, cayenne pepper to taste....next time no salt. I mixed the rue in the spinach and broth aND then blended most of it. Turned out to be a beautiful color and very flavorful! This is a keeper of a soup recipe!

A great way to get your veggies! I used chicken broth instead of water and bouillon, a 10oz bag of fresh spinach leaves instead of frozen, half of a small/medium yellow onion instead of dried onion, and cornstarch instead of flour, to make it gluten-free. I cooked the spinach whole, but I used a submersion blender to chop up the spinach and onions just before serving. It was delicious!

Following the recipe as is I would only rate this 3 out of 5 stars. Do the following and its definately a 5 star recipe. I thought it was too plain. Take out the water and bouilloon; use chicken broth instead (better & fuller flavor) Use 2 cups of half & half and 1 cup of milk. Substitute 1/4 cup fresh minced onion instead of dried. Add 2 cup of shredded swiss cheese. 1. Saute onion in butter in large saucepan until onion is soft. 2. Add 1/4 c flour, wisk with butter and onion until well mixed. Pour in chicken broth, wisking rapidly to ensure everything mixes well. 3. Add spinach. Bring to a boil. 4. Add cream & milk. 5. Add cheese, stirring constantly until all cheese is melted. 6. Season to taste. (I also added two drops of roasted habinaro sauce which has a really nice flavor without making it spicy. I hate black pepper so I use other peppers) This soup was very filling and delicious.

Steamed frozen broccoli in chicken broth. Sautéed garlic and shallot in butter. Added red pepper flakes. After softened, wisked in whole wheat pastry flour. Poured in chicken broth with broccoli, 2 1/2 cups almond milk, 1/2 cup organic half and half and 1 can of white kidney beans. Liquified with emulsion blender. Salt and pepper. Topped with freshly grated Parmesan. Delicious! Next time I think I may only emulsify half, add some ham or bacon and use olive oil instead of butter!

Just made this in about 20 minutes. Fast, easy and delicious. I used a can of chicken broth and mixed in a half onion chopped and the garlic to cook with the spinach. I then put that mixture in the blender to make it smooth. I used 3 cups of skim milk and it turned out very creamy, whisking the butter, flour and milk until almost boiling, but not scalding the milk. Then I poured the blended spinach mixture into the butter, flour, milk mixture, turned off the heat, added some cayenne and celery salt. Tastes great!

This soup is delicious! I made a few changes based on other reviews: I added some garlic powder (I always do), I subbed one of the cups of milk for a cup of heavy cream, and I used an immersion blender at the end. The flavor was wonderful and it was quick and easy to make.

I had a BIG Costco bag of fresh spinach which I wanted to make a dent in so I chopped up about a pound or so. I did this in one pot. I sauteed 1/2 an onion in some EVOO until it began to brown & added 1 clove garlic & a dash of red pepper flakes,added butter to pot and about 3 T flour and cooked for about 2-3 minutes. Added 1 can chicken broth, spinach & cut back to 2 cups 1/2 n 1/2 so it would be thicker. Let is simmer a few minutes until the spinach was soft then went into pot with my immersion blender but left some of the texture...delish.

First, my result looked nothing like the picture, which is very green and almost looks like a puree! Mine is creamy looking with spinach green mottled throughout! I used the recipe with these changes and additions (based somewhat on reviews). I did use bouillon cubes, but added a little garlic powder. I cooked 2 small boxes (10 oz ?) of chopped frozen spinach, and used slightly more than one for the recipe, and all the water, saving back about a drained cup for later use (omelettes perhaps). I sauteed about two TBL of finely minced Vidalia onion in the butter along with just a tad of minced garlic (from a jar). I forgot I had the minced garlic and had already added garlic powder, so I did not want to overdo it. I used only 2 1/2 cups of milk and whisked in 1/2 block (4 oz) of yogurt cream cheese. I did this because I had it on hand, but it was expiring soon, and I thought it might add some depth. It took a while to get the cream cheese whisked in. The results, I thought, were fantastic! The best thing is it has none of those "additives" you see in canned cream soups. I'm glad I did not double the recipe though, as this makes a lot of soup for one person.
Made as directed. Soooo good! Easy peasy.
Love my mom had a old recipe but I don't remember it.shes from the 40s
It was really easy to make and shared with co-worker who loved it as well!!
this is an awesome recipe! Thank you!

This soup was excellent and ridiculously easy. I had everything measured out in advance and it came together is less than 15 minutes. My husband and I do not love spinach but both agreed this was excellent. We also both agreed that it tasted "cheesy" even though the recipe does not have cheese in it. I added red pepper flakes but only because I like some kick with my spinach. This one is a keeper and I'm already looking forward to making it again.
